articles.title: Chinese swimmer Zhang Zhanshuo completes sweep of seven gold medals at the Asian Games
articles.summary: Chinese freestyler Zhang Zhanshuo completed his sweep of seven gold medals at the Asian Games, taking the 400-meter freestyle in 3 minutes, 41.28 seconds on...
articles.body:
NAGOYA, Japan (AP) — Chinese freestyler Zhang Zhanshuo completed his sweep of seven gold medals at the Asian Games , taking the 400-meter freestyle in 3 minutes, 41.28 seconds on Friday on the final day of swimming events.

His time was just 1.30 seconds off the world record held by Lukas Martens of Germany (3:39.98).

Zhang also won the 1,500, 800 and 200 free and added gold in three relays.

He celebrated at poolside by sitting on the lane divider and counting the golds with his fingers.

China claims a record gold haul in the meet

The Chinese won a record 30 gold medals — and 54 overall — during the six days of swimming at these Asian Games and surpassed the 28 gold medals they won three years ago in Hangzhou.

Japan was right there in many races, winning seven gold and 37 medals overall — also better than their totals three years ago.

Japan's 17-year-old Shin Ohashi set the only world record of the games, taking the 200-meter breaststroke on Thursday in 2:04.83. Ohashi obliterated the old mark of 2:05.48 set by China's Qin Haiyang in 2023 at the world championships in Fukuoka, Japan.

China's 13-year-old Yu Zidi was the most talked about swimmer heading into the Asian Games. She did not disappoint, winning the 200 butterfly, and the 200 and 400 individual medleys.

Her time in the 200 IM was 2:06.10, just off the world mark held by Canadian Summer McIntosh (2:05.70).

Yu's times are still a bit off McIntosh's standard in all three events. But she is a legitimate threat at next year's world championships and the 2028 Olympics where, of course, other swim powers like Australia and United States will be present.

China won gold medals in five of the seven races on Friday, just as dominant as it was all week.

Zhang Yufei won the women's 50 fly in 25.41 with teammate Wu Qingfeng taking silver. China's Qin Haiyang took the 50 breaststroke (26.68) with Ohashi — the record-setter on Thursday — settling for bronze.

Other Chinese winners were Li Bingjie in the 800 free (8:24.02), Zhang Zhanshuo in the 400 free (3:41.28), and the women's 4x100 medley relay (3:54.55).

Japan's Kodai Nishiono won the men's 200 backstroke (1:56.42), and Taiwan's Wang Kuan-hung claimed the 200 fly (1:55.05).

articles.title: Karra Elejalde, Kandido Uranga, el cine... y la petanca: "Se trata mal a los abueletes"
articles.standfirst: Presentado en San Sebastián 'El Triplete', cortometraje protagonizado por los dos actores, escrito y dirigido por Rodrigo Olmedo y ganador de la sexta edición del Audi Future Stories
articles.summary: Presentado en San Sebastián 'El Triplete', cortometraje protagonizado por los dos actores, escrito y dirigido por Rodrigo Olmedo y ganador de la sexta edición del Audi Future Stories
articles.body: Antonio y Mariano son dos amigos, de 75 y 78 años, que viven en una residencia de ancianos y que, tras perder a Ezequiel, el tercer miembro de su equipo de petanca, descubren que sus cenizas irán a un cenicero común. Para evitarlo y cumplir una última promesa... Hasta ahí se puede (y se debe) contar. Porque 'El Triplete', cortometraje ganador de la sexta edición del certamen Audi Future Stories, fue presentado este viernes en el marco del Festival de Cine de San Sebastián... justo antes de llegar a las correspondientes plataformas. Conviene atender a la petanca, siquiera sea durante un párrafo, que por ahí viene la relación establecida entre el guion de Rodrigo Olmedo y el mundo del deporte. Aclara la propia web de la Federación española que "el origen de los juegos de bolas se remonta a la noche de los tiempos", aunque por lo visto fueron los romanos quienes "privilegiaron la habilidad con la idea de un objetivo al que había que aproximarse". Hasta 1907, en todo caso, no nació el juego sin impulso, entendido como verdadera petanca. Su nombre vendría de la expresión 'pieds tanquees'. En castellano, pies plantados. Pero la historia primero escrita y después dirigida por Rodrigo Olmedo exhibe mucho más que petanca: tiene elementos de 'road movie', ofrece ironía en dosis adecuada... e invita a una necesaria reflexión sobre el papel de la tercera edad. A la que en teoría pertenecen Karra Elejalde y Kandido Uranga, protagonistas del corto (con Biel Durán completando elenco). El primero, con sus dos Goya como actor de reparto a cuestas (por 'También la lluvia' y por 'Ocho apellidos vascos') y haciendo doblete en el Festival ('Arriba Tutto', de José Mota); el segundo, con el 'pelotazo' que ha supuesto tras una extensa trayectora la reciente 'Maspalomas'. Karra y Kandido se sientan con MARCA para lo que se supone será entrevista pero, las cosas como son, termina siendo divertida charla entre ellos... - "La verdad es que nunca habíamos jugado a la petanca" - "Pero es muy intenso, ¿eh?" - "Sí, pero rodando nunca tienes tiempo. Bueno, delante nuestro tiraron dos que juegan y observamos cómo lo hacían, nada más. No ha sido 'voy a ir a un cursillo o a que alguien nos enseñe'. Hemos visto mil veces a los abueletes y sabemos que consiste en que tu bola tiene que estar lo más cerca del boliche, ¿no? Entonces, pues lo intentas..." Kandido quería ser pelotari o futbolista: "Y he salido actor. Ni ganando, ni perdiendo. El azar o la necesidad me han traído por este camino, pero también he descubierto que hubiera podido ser muchísimas cosas más. Como cualquier persona, salvo la que esté obcecada en algo. Pero eso de pelotari, pues era una cosa infantil. Lo dices porque entonces se te da bien el deporte y ése es el que praticas, no la petanca". Karra tira por el basket: "Yo he vivido la mitad de mi vida en Vitoria. Y el Alavés no nos daba grandes satisfacciones, pero el Baskonia sí. Entonces, pues a través de eso vas conociendo jugadores, que si Rivas, que si Arlauckas, y acabas viendo NBA. Pero mira, yo de crío quería ser pelotari... o cura. Y me decía mi 'ama' que ni loco. Es que venían frailes al colegio y nos ponían diapositivas de cómo los niños del Orinoco estaban ahí con las tripitas hinchadas, bañándose en bolas con los cocodrilos y la hostia. Venían a captarte para ser misionero, yo qué sé, agustinos, jesuitas, marianistas... Cada fraile traía un hábito y un color distintos. Y yo decía en casa que quería irme porque lo que quería era aventuras". - P. "¿Qué encontrará el público en 'El Triplete'?" - "A Karra, a mí... y las cenizas de Ezequiel". - "Un corto simpático que yo creo que es un homenaje a la amistad, a la lealtad o a los valores. Y también hay algo de rebeldía, ¿sabes? Son dos abuelos que están en una residencia, pero, me cago en la leche, todavía tienen energía suficiente para crearle problemas al director". - "¿Sabes por qué? Porque, mira, ayer me desperté... y habían pasado 40 años". - "¿En serio?" - "Y todo por hacer. Eso es lo que nos pasa". - P. "¿Cómo se trata a la tercera edad?" - "Mal, cada vez peor. Estamos apartando a los abueletes. O sea, antes un viejillo iba al banco, a la ventanilla, y decía: 'Quiero 50 euros'. El otro día vi como le decían a una: 'Señora, que tiene el cajero... ¿Tiene tarjeta?' 'Sí, pero...' '¿Sabe la clave?' 'No me acuerdo'. Y como de malas maneras... Tío, ¿qué te pasa? Ahora un abuelo se quiere borrar de lo que sea y le dicen que mande un correo, que los operadores están ocupados. Después le mandan una clave que no se sabe si es un 6 o una G... una mierda. La tecnología está haciendo que apartemos a los abuelos de la vida". - "No sólo la tecnología. Los tecnócratas, con nombres y apellidos. O sea, los que administran, los que dicen cómo tienen que ser las cosas. Normalmente una persona muy lista, salida de la universidad, entre 30 y 50 años, que ha decidido que para facilitar y para ahorrar personal se necesita por ejemplo un chip para abrir la basura... De locos". - "Una persona de 80 o 90 años a día de hoy se encuentra con problemas técnicos en la vida cotidiana. Y no han tenido tiempo para adaptarse o no les ha salido de los huevos. Yo no tengo Facebook o no tengo Instagram y mi chica me dice: '¿Cómo alardeas de eso, puto animal?' Yo soy analógico total". - "Y fumas..." - "Y fumo. Sí, señor". - "Yo hasta hace poco..." Kandido lleva la conversación incluso a los desahucios: "Es que me da vergüenza hablar. Prefiero no decir nada, porque eso es muy fácil. ¿No estamos todos un poco hartos de hablar? ¿Qué hacemos? ¿A dónde llegamos? No llegamos a ningún sitio, creo que ni manifestándonos... ¡Qué vergüenza! Yo tengo mucho pudor de llevar cualquier pin o de hacer cualquier denuncia. Es jodido todo esto. Sólo me quedan la melancolía o la nostalgia". "Por eso digo", interviene Karra, "que en el contexto del corto hay un homenaje a la lealtad y también un poco de rebeldía. Yo no quiero ni saber a cuántos abueletes los arruinan en las residencias. ¡A mí qué no me lleven! Que me tiren por un agujero antes". - "Se puede decir que se rebelan, pero también simplemente que quieren vivir. Y vivir es reír, es compartir... y si tienen que enfrentarse a alguien lo hacen, pero no por rebelarse, sino por vivir. Lo de antes parece un chiste, pero no lo es: 'Ayer me levanté, pasaron 40 años y tengo todo por hacer'. Eso me pasa a mí ahora con 71 años y reivindico que tengo todo por hacer. Nos queda toda la vida por delante". Que así sea.

articles.title: 17.17m and onto the podium: Manpreet Kaur makes history; wins women's shot put bronze at Asian Games
articles.summary: Indian shot putter Manpreet Kaur made history on Friday by winning the bronze medal in the women's shot put final at the 2026 Asian Games in Nagoya.
articles.body: Indian shot putter Manpreet Kaur made history on Friday by winning the bronze medal in the women's shot put final at the 2026 Asian Games in Nagoya.The 36-year-old became only the third Indian woman to win an Asian Games medal in women's shot put.Manpreet secured bronze with a best throw of 17.17m, winning her first Asian Games medal. She opened with a throw of 16.32m and improved with each round before producing her medal-winning effort in the fourth round.She fouled her sixth and final attempt, but it did not affect the result as she remained third in the field.The 36-year-old Manpreet hails from Patiala and her last major international performance was a bronze at the 2023 Asian Championships. Her personal best is 18.06m that came in 2022.The bronze marks a return to the podium for Manpreet after more than a decade at the senior level. She returned to competition in 2021 after serving a four-year doping ban.At the previous Asian Games in Hangzhou, Manpreet finished fifth. Earlier this year, she narrowly missed a medal at the 2026 Commonwealth Games after finishing fourth with a throw of 17.49m.India's other finalist, Krishna Jayasankar, finished fifth with a best throw of 16.57m.China's Jiayuan Song won the gold medal with a throw of 19.40m, while China's Linru Zhang took silver with 18.14m. Manpreet's 17.17m was enough to secure bronze for India.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: A’ja Wilson’s massive collision with a WNBA worker goes viral as footage captures unexpected off-court moment involving Aces superstar
articles.summary: A'ja Wilson's collision with an arena worker turned into the most-talked-about clip out of Las Vegas' regular season finale.
articles.body: A'ja Wilson's collision with an arena worker turned into the most-talked-about clip out of Las Vegas' regular season finale. The Aces star was moving at full speed near the sideline just before tip-off when she ran straight into a staffer who never saw her coming, and the two went down together in a moment that had fans arguing over whether it counted as a block or a charge.Neither Wilson nor the worker was seriously hurt, and the footage has already crossed nearly two million views since it hit social media early Friday. Las Vegas, for its part, barely blinked, closing out the finale in dominant fashion and setting up a playoff run that starts this weekend against a familiar rival.A'ja Wilson's massive collision with WNBA worker goes viralIt happened just before the Aces tipped off their regular season finale. Wilson, the two-time reigning MVP, was hustling along the baseline when she plowed into the unsuspecting worker, sending her sprawling. The crowd gasped for a second before it became clear both were fine and able to walk it off.Sports commentator Joshua Sánchez posted the clip on X, captioning it, "A'ja Wilson… Block or Charge? 💀😭 #WNBA #RaiseTheStakes." The post has racked up close to two million views in less than a day, turning a routine pregame moment into one of the WNBA's bigger social media stories of the week.Once the ball actually went up, Las Vegas jumped out to a 32-18 lead and never let go, closing out a 100-82 win. That victory locked up the No. 3 seed for the Aces, who now carry a seven-game winning streak straight into the postseason.A'ja Wilson is set to face Caitlin Clark heading into the playoffsThe win sent Las Vegas into a first-round matchup with Caitlin Clark and the Indiana Fever, who slid to the No. 6 seed after an 86-66 loss to Minnesota on Thursday while Washington and Golden State both won. It sets up a rematch of last year's semifinals, a series the Aces closed out in five games without Clark on the floor at all.This time Clark is healthy, and Indiana actually won this year's regular-season series 2-1. The picture is messier than that record suggests, though. The Fever blew out Las Vegas twice, once with both stars sitting and once with Clark playing well, but the Aces took the rubber match in August behind an overtime performance from Chelsea Gray, who hit a three to force extra time and another to close it. Wilson had 26 points, 13 rebounds and the defensive stop on Clark that set up Gray's game-winner.Wilson is chasing her fifth MVP after averaging 26.2 points, 9.4 rebounds, 3.2 assists, 1.9 blocks and 1.4 steals a game this season. Jackie Young is putting up 19.3 points and 6.7 assists, and Gray, at 33, is still handing out 6.6 assists a night. Indiana will counter with Kelsey Mitchell, who finished second in the league in scoring at 25 points a game and set a WNBA record with 27 straight 20-point outings, plus Clark, who tied for the league lead in assists at 8.5 per game. Injuries to Aliyah Boston and Ty Harris cloud how much of that firepower Indiana can actually use.Game 1 tips off Sunday in Las Vegas, with the time still to be announced.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua are set to finally meet in one of the biggest heavyweight fights in British boxing.
articles.body: Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua are set to finally meet in one of the biggest heavyweight fights in British boxing. The long-awaited clash is scheduled for Friday, December 11, at Cardiff’s Principality Stadium, with the main event expected to take place in the early hours of the morning in the UK.While the heavyweight rivals will headline the show, several major names are being linked with the undercard. Manny Pacquiao is reportedly being considered for a huge cross-generational fight with Shakur Stevenson. Other possible bouts could feature Filip Hrgovic, Rico Verhoeven and Jack Catterall, although the undercard remains subject to official confirmation.Manny Pacquiao and other big names linked to Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua undercardNetflix is reportedly keen to make Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua a major event for its American audience. That has led to speculation about a high-profile co-main event featuring Manny Pacquiao and Shakur Stevenson.Pacquiao, 47, is one of boxing’s biggest stars. The Filipino legend became the first boxer to win world titles in eight different weight divisions. articles.title: George Russell takes Azerbaijan GP pole by eight tenths as Leclerc admits gap was unexpected
articles.summary: George Russell reckons beating Charles Leclerc to pole position in the Azerbaijan GP "was probably the biggest margin of [his] whole career". The Mercedes dr...
articles.body:
George Russell reckons beating Charles Leclerc to pole position in the Azerbaijan GP "was probably the biggest margin of [his] whole career".

The Mercedes driver said the margin was "sweet", while Leclerc acknowledged that Ferrari had not expected to be so far behind.

"It has been a while so definitely feels good," said Russell. "It's probably the biggest margin of my whole career, even including F2 and F3 days.

"The lap felt really sweet. The car has been feeling great this weekend and on a track like this when you can hook it up like that it feels really amazing."

Russell credited both the car's form and the timing of his final run. A gap to Isack Hadjar ahead gave him a slipstream along the back straight, which Russell believed was worth a little extra time. It was an advantage he made count in a session where the scale of his lead became the story.

"It was just the perfect lap at the end. I was in a good gap behind to Hadjar, which gave me a nice little slipstream probably by another tenth or two down this backstraight, so it was great," he added.

Leclerc happy with second spot on the grid

Leclerc was satisfied with much of his own final attempt, but the gap to pole left him questioning whether he could have found more. After a difficult start to the weekend, Ferrari had gained some encouragement before qualifying. The result met Leclerc's expectations in terms of grid position, but not in terms of outright pace.

"Honestly, it was quite a good lap. Lewis was three-four seconds, I think, in front, and I managed to do a good lap at the end. But when I see the gap to George, maybe the lap wasn't good enough.

"Overall, we've been on the back foot all weekend. We kind of expected to be very far off after a difficult Thursday, but this morning I had a little bit more hope.

"I think in terms of position, that's where we expected to be, but in terms of gap it's a lot more than what we expected.

"We'll see tomorrow. Our straight-line speed is not our strength but the pace has been quite strong in FP1 for high-fuel, so I hope that will be the case tomorrow."

The result capped a sharply contrasting qualifying session for Mercedes. While Russell secured pole, team-mate Kimi Antonelli hit the wall at Turn 1 in Q1, damaging the front-left corner of his car. He was unable to take part in Q2 and qualified 16th, leaving him with a difficult recovery ahead.

Elsewhere, both Alpine drivers, Pierre Gasly and Franco Colapinto, reached the top-ten shootout. Carlos Sainz also made Q3 for Williams, giving each a chance to start near the front of the midfield.

Russell, though, leaves qualifying with the clearest advantage. His lap put him eight tenths ahead of the field; the next challenge is turning that pace into a race result.

articles.title: Miami Heat Linked to Damian Lillard, 4 More Potential Targets
articles.summary: The Miami Heat took a significant step forward this offseason after trading for Giannis Antetokounmpo, but questions remain about the team’s backcourt headin...
articles.body:
The Miami Heat took a significant step forward this offseason after trading for Giannis Antetokounmpo , but questions remain about the team's backcourt heading into the year.

Why Miami Might Look Beyond Davion Mitchell

While Giannis and Bam Adebayo figure to anchor the frontcourt, Miami still lacks a true floor general to run the offense at an elite level. Davion Mitchell, 28, currently holds that role. There's growing uncertainty about whether the Heat plan to commit to him long-term, according to Barry Jackson of the Miami Herald.

Jackson reported that Miami may prefer to wait and see how Mitchell fits alongside Antetokounmpo this season. The team is also keeping an eye on which free agents might accept the Heat's mid-level exception next summer. Mitchell has just one year and $12.4 million remaining on his contract. That puts real weight on how he performs. He averaged 9.3 points, 2.7 rebounds and 6.5 assists per game last season. Improving on those numbers could be enough to secure a bigger long-term deal.

Lillard stands out as the most notable name given his history of interest in joining Miami previously, though his age and recent injury concerns have diminished his overall value somewhat. LaVine represents a different kind of fit as more of a scoring guard than a traditional playmaker, and as a two-time All-Star who just turned 31, he could also land outside what Miami is realistically able to offer. Hunter, DiVincenzo and Dort round out the list as more affordable, modest additions, each bringing versatility at the guard spot without requiring major financial commitment.

For now, Miami appears content with its roster as constructed, even while acknowledging room for improvement at the position. If Mitchell develops into the player the team hopes he can become, the Heat would likely be satisfied extending him and moving on from the search entirely. Until that happens, though, the organization is expected to keep exploring its options given the win-now timeline created by the Antetokounmpo trade.

articles.title: 'Workhorse' Koumas growing with Wales
articles.summary: Liverpool forward Lewis Koumas earns praise from Wales boss Craig Bellamy and full-back Neco Williams following his efforts against Portugal.
articles.body:
One swing of a left boot had Wales fans dreaming of a shock outcome in Portugal .

It was ultimately not to be for Lewis Koumas whose close-range shot was brilliantly blocked on the line by Manchester City defender Ruben Dias in the 74th minute.

But it was yet another example of the Liverpool forward giving the Red Wall an emotion they had probably not expected to feel in Lisbon. Genuine hope.

Without a number of key players at Estadio Jose Alvalade, Craig Bellamy hoped the contest with the defending Nations League champions would help Wales find "the next Harry Wilson ".

Despite a 1-0 loss, the fixture provided more evidence that Koumas is ready to be the man Wales can depend on.

"The positive part is you expose one or two players to this moment, I remember doing it about two years ago in Turkey with Koumas," Bellamy said.

"I thought he was outstanding and I'm thinking, 'he belongs here'."

The 21-year-old's work-rate was contagious, and his quality on the ball appears significantly advanced to what it was even just a year or so ago.

It is no wonder Andoni Iraola felt the need to keep Koumas at Liverpool this season following his previous loans at Stoke City, Birmingham City and Hull City.

"They kept him on at Anfield. You don't get the choice to stay," Bellamy said of Koumas remaining with the Reds.

"If they want to keep you, they keep you. It's a difference."

Koumas' efforts have not gone unnoticed in the Wales camp either.

Nottingham Forest full-back Neco Williams knows how difficult it is to make the grade at Liverpool, having left the Merseyside outfit in 2022 in search of more regular minutes.

But Williams has already seen enough from Koumas to feel confident that the future is bright as far as the youngster is concerned.

"His confidence is growing each game," said Williams.

"The more games he plays, the older he gets, the more experience he gets, he'll become better and better.

"What I see with him is he's improving all the time. He's a workhorse, he doesn't stop working, and they're the type of players you want in your team."

With games against Denmark and Norway to come in the first international window of the season, Koumas will have further opportunities to stake his claim in a Wales shirt.

But as the evidence of his ability to shine for the Red Dragons continues to build, Bellamy can no doubt rest assured that he has the kind of talent he has so desperately craved at his disposal when it comes to the young forward.

articles.title: Raul Rosas Jr. developing game plan to finish Raoni Barcelos
articles.summary: Raul Rosas Jr. has been developing a game plan and plans to finish Raoni Barcelos this weekend.
articles.body:
Raul Rosas Jr. believes he has developed a game plan that will help him secure a finish on Saturday night.

With an extraordinary age gap, Rosas Jr. will face Raoni Barcelos ; almost an incredible 18 years between them. At different stages of their careers, both men are riding high and bring a combined 10-fight win streak into the octagon when they collide this weekend. But somebody's run has reached its end, and Rosas Jr. believes he will be the one to get his hand raised.

Despite last losing over three years ago, Raul Rosas Jr. is confident that he and his team have developed a game plan to stop the Brazilian's late-career surge. The 21-year-old said:

"Usually, we'll study tape, and I'll give my opinion, like, 'This is how I can fight him.' And with all my team, we discuss. They're like, 'Okay, maybe, yeah. But do this.' So we just put it all together. So, now we have a game plan, and this is to me the funnest part of the week, you know. Going out there and trying to see if it works."

Game planning has worked for Raul Rosas Jr. throughout his early UFC career. During his last outing, Rosas Jr. earned a unanimous decision victory over Rob Font . Throughout the matchup, the prospect utilized a grapple-heavy approach, knowing Font's strengths and weaknesses.

Disappointed with himself at not getting a finish this time, Rosas Jr. wants to amend his shortcomings with an eye-catching performance at the Meta APEX on Saturday.

"I studied a lot of fights, and I just knew- I knew it was going to play in that way; that it was going to be not so hard for me to get him to the ground because I saw Cory Sandhagen and Jean Matsumoto [do it], and I just knew that they didn't have the grappling that I have."

"So, I was like, if I get to those positions, I think he won't be able to get up. I would have liked the finish, but here we are, and we're going to get a finish this Saturday."

articles.title: Nuggets reportedly interested in signing $2M ex-Mavericks crafty guard to pair with Nikola Jokic
articles.summary: The Denver Nuggets have already recently made a two-way deal. It looks like they are eyeing their next potential two-way contract.
articles.body:
The Charlotte Hornets have made several moves this summer, including trading former franchise star LaMelo Ball to the Minnesota Timberwolves . This marked the beginning of a new era in Charlotte, as the team looks to give its younger talent more responsibility.

"Among our latest items, Atlanta and Charlotte have held trade talks surrounding Buddy Hield for Dorian Finney-Smith , sources say. It remains unclear whether an agreement will be struck before training camps open," Bleacher Report's Jake Fischer posted.

This was a trade that could have worked for both sides, as it would have allowed Charlotte to add another shooter to its roster. On Tuesday, the deal between the two teams became official.

"The Atlanta Hawks are trading Buddy Hield, Ryan Nembhard and cash considerations to the Charlotte Hornets for Dorian Finney-Smith, the team announced on Tuesday. The Hornets are expected to waive Nembhard as part of the trade, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania," ESPN's Ohm Youngmisuk wrote.

With Nembhard likely to be waived by the Hornets, he could have some options if he clears waivers. The Denver Nuggets are reportedly one team highly interested in giving him a contract.

"The Nuggets, meanwhile, remain prominent among various teams with two-way deal interest in Ryan Nembhard, league sources say. Nembhard has not yet been officially waived by Charlotte but is expected to focus on teams with a backup point guard need if he indeed clears waivers," The Stein Line's Marc Stein posted.

At the very least, Nembhard would have the opportunity to learn from players such as Nikola Jokic and, especially, guard Jamal Murray . Nembhard is a crafty guard who is simply looking for the right fit to showcase his abilities.

He is currently on a $2 million contract , and Denver is looking to make a deep postseason run. While signing Nembhard wouldn't be a major addition, it could still pay dividends for the Nuggets during the regular season.

articles.title: Game 4 Preview: Clemson Travels West to Face California on Friday Night
articles.summary: Can the Tigers Build on the End of the UNC Game? I decided this week to start with a little good, bad, and ugly from the previous week before I jump into the...
articles.body:
Can the Tigers Build on the End of the UNC Game?

I decided this week to start with a little good, bad, and ugly from the previous week before I jump into the preview for this upcoming game. The UNC game was certainly a roller coaster ride both with the game and with the weather, but the back end of the game offered several glimmers of hope that this team can become something good.

The GOOD: Clemson's secondary continues to shine and if the front can just start making teams have to throw it more, this defense could really make strides. Big if right now though. Tait Reynolds really came on as the game progressed and flashed what makes you excited for what he can become. Gideon Davidson showed why he is RB1 and we started to see what Chad Morris can dial up if he can just get some kind of OL play established. Nolan Hauser continues to nail kicks and CJ Johnson showed he is a dangerous return man.

The BAD: Clemson's offense left a lot to be desired again throughout most of the first half. Even when they dialed up a perfect play, like the under screen to Wesco (same play LSU used on us in the first game), the ball wasn't great and Wesco dropped it. Seeing it on film revealed just how open that was for a huge gain. Some of the pass protection also was problematic with some of the interior guards getting beat 1 on 1 for sacks or pressures. UNC didn't blitz nearly as much as LSU so

The UGLY: Clemson struggled mightily out of the gate and throughout most of the game with UNC's stretch zone runs and some of the play action that came off of it. The Clemson DL got owned a good bit, especially inside, and that certainly has to change if the Tigers hope to make 2026 better than 2025. I will also rank Saturday in the top 3 or 4 hottest days in Death Valley I can remember. It was brutal ahead of the weather delay that sent me and most everyone else back to shade or air conditioning.

Now the Tigers look to get to 2-0 in ACC play. This is extremely important with the Miami Hurricanes due to come to town the week after. Like UNC, California doesn't scare you across the board but they certainly have enough to beat Clemson, especially the version that we saw in the first quarter and a half vs. UNC and the entire game at LSU.

Clemson Offense vs. California Defense: I have to say I got very excited to start seeing some of the things Chad Morris dialed up once the Tigers finally got some adequate OL play and some run game going. Clemson probably should have had at least two more explosive pass plays to Wesco if the throws and catches had been better. Reynolds was very shaky early, but the third down conversion he made on the last drive of the second quarter was big time and he was good from there other than the interception on the missed bomb. Had to love the man child stiff arm on his one run that showed he's not your typical QB in that regard. The tight ends came alive also, which is the byproduct of the run game finding some success. Clemson is going to need the offense to help the defense this year because it is hard to imagine the DL making huge leaps from what we have seen against major D1 OL personnel. Cal's defense has not been terrific to this point against power conference competition. They gave up over 400 yards to both UCLA and Syracuse, but at least they kept Syracuse under 20 points and turned them over 3 times on picks. They got to feast on Wagner last week which I'm sure they hope is a sign they are getting better themselves. I admit I haven't watched a lot of Cal this season, but I seriously doubt they have DL as good as UNC had last week. Clemson needs to carry that OL play over where we definitely saw guys being physical and getting hats on hats way beyond anything we've seen since probably 2023 or 2024. Davidson's TD run was a thing of beauty.

The Riley era often felt like one step forward and two steps back. That stretch in 2024 before Mafah got hurt was the closest to consistency we saw. Now Morris is on the clock to see if the offense can build on the success or revert to some of the same issues that had the wheels spinning in the mud. If the bomb to Wesco against App State was the cathartic moment that got the 24 team going, perhaps that Tyler Brown reverse TD last week will be the one for the Tigers in 26. Clemson used more OL this past week and it had to have helped. O'Connell was one with a key block on Davidson's TD run, and maybe spending some time on the sideline watching Grant Wise take snaps lit a fire under him. It certainly became evident that once Clemson could run the ball, the WR and TE group got a lot more dangerous. Clemson survived the two turnovers last week by getting two of their own, but ball security is going to be huge this week because Syracuse no doubt beats Cal two weeks ago if not for the turnovers. They have better secondary pieces than UNC but are not as good up front as UNC. Clemson needs to punish that with the run game on Friday night the way teams have tried to punish Clemson in the same way.

Do you want to support STS writers? You can do so by supporting our sponsor, Section 103. Just saying my Section 103 Polo is officially 1-0 after last week's game. They deep dive school traditions to create thoughtful designs artfully applied to insanely comfortable tees, polos, hats, and more. Be sure to use our promo code STS10 so you get 10% off your first order and we get credit for sending you their way. Their founder, Steven, has been good to us and we think you'll love their Clemson merch. Click here to explore.

Clemson Defense vs. California Offense: As I noted earlier, there is a lot to like about the Clemson secondary. UNC had very little success through the air and what they did get was mostly to tight ends or running backs. Ashton Hampton has the Nate Wiggins #2 this year and is playing a lot like Nate did in 2023. Elliot Washington iced the game with a pick and Corey Myrick played the 4th and 1 play action shot perfectly. However, Clemson's front had all kinds of issues with UNC's power run game and stretch zone. That stretch play has given the Tigers fits for a while now, mainly from Louisville, but both LSU and UNC employed it to great effect this year. Clemson also struggled with middle pressure which allowed Tarheel QB Billy Edwards to scramble for some easy first downs early on. This got better as the game went and Tom Allen got increasingly more aggressive with blitz calls. This reminded me of the Reggie Herring style of run defense, which was to bring numbers early and often. That put a ton of pressure on Herring's secondary which got burned more and more before he departed after the 2001 defense got lit up all year long. This secondary can hold up against most everyone but the front has to contain the QB and, of course, do better at stopping the primary run game. It doesn't help that the DT room will be without another main contributor as Devarrick Woods has been ruled out along with starting nickel Corian Gipson. Clemson now has three of its top 5 DTs out with injuries and will need Vic Burley to come around even more quickly as a result.

California has a great QB in Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele, but as good as he is, stopping the Cal run game and primary back Adam Mohammed has to be top priority. Mohammed has rushed for at least 74 yards in all three games this season. They don't have the depth at RB that UNC enjoyed, but Mohammed is a dangerous runner and has to be accounted for to prevent Cal from being able to employ all their play action schemes. California's OL will be the worst Clemson has faced this season outside of maybe Georgia Southern, but their skill at QB and RB helps mask some of that. Will Heldt has come on and is up to 4 sacks and 6.5 TFLs already, but the guy I'm getting excited about is London Merritt who helped put a stop to the UNC run game by setting the edge like it is supposed to be set. Merritt has flashed in all three games and is seeing his snap load increase as a result.

UNC's passing attack was rendered helpless once Clemson finally got a handle on their running game. As Clemson has learned the hard way, slipping the RB or TE out for pass plays isn't nearly as easy if the run game hasn't set it up. Clemson's alpha corners make life difficult for any outside WR and the upgrades at safety have led to seeing QBs have to hold the ball more than they did last year at any point. As long as the rush doesn't allow escapes like Sam Leavitt feasted on, QBs are going to have to be extremely accurate and on time more often than not this season. JKS has got the goods to do that but the Tigers have to force him to be superman and see how it goes.

Special Teams: Clemson certainly experienced the Ray Guy treatment from UNC's punter and Jack Smith is a lot better at punting balls high than far, but otherwise you have to like the contributions from this unit which have been consistently getting it done. Nolan Hauser is an early MVP candidate (which you hope changes, of course, due to others ramping up production). Clemson's go ahead TD drive was boosted by a good kick return by Chris Johnson Jr. Most importantly, there have been no disasters which this current Clemson team is not equipped to overcome at this point. Knock on wood that continues this week on the west coast.

Overall: It is hard to figure how the team will look flying across the country and playing in a new environment. Clemson was simply awful in Baton Rouge from about the second series of the game. However, that trip has to certainly help with this one as this stage won't nearly be as daunting as that one. Clemson has also dealt with all the delays that have pushed games deep into the night on two occasions. But we've seen teams go west and lay eggs like Florida State, Louisville, and SMU last year. Both the Cards and especially the Mustangs cost themselves trips to Charlotte mostly from those failures. Clemson is a long way from thinking about Charlotte, but getting to 2-0 before that daunting Miami game seems essential to any type of successful season. I'm anxious to see if the Tigers (especially offensively) truly turned a corner last week.

articles.title: Alabama Football 2026: Previewing the South Carolina Defense
articles.summary: Dylan Stewart Returns!
articles.body:
While Shane Beamer keeps changing out his offensive coordinator like an air filter, he's stuck with defensive coordinator Clayton White ever since 2021. 6 straight years is a long time. At this point, you generally know the scheme: it's a multiple front, 1-gap defense that goes with a whole lot of man coverage with plenty of blitzing, and there's a big focus on getting the edge rushers into 1v1 matchups with offensive tackles and letting them do their thing.

The Gamecocks generally took care of business in their two season-opener warm up games, shutting out Kent State and only allowing 9 points to Towson. Unfortunately for them, their SEC opener was against the notorious buzzsaw named Mississippi State .

Now, MSU is looking a bit surprising with Kamario Taylor at QB and garnering quite a bit of hype…. But the Gamecocks allowed 41 points in that game, generally looking lost and overwhelmed the whole game. It wasn't pretty (and also I'm not sure just how much love MSU really should be getting just yet).

The real linchpin to things for USC is edge rusher Dylan Stewart . The junior has been touted as a future top-ten draft pick for two years now for his otherworldly athleticism and length on the edge. Unfortunately, he missed the end of last season and the first two games of this season with a lingering back injury. He did finally get to take some snaps last week vs Mississippi State, but was on a limited pitch count. It sounds like they expect him to be ramping up to a heavier workload against Alabama this week, but there will likely be some rust for him to shake off.

Caleb Herring and Anthony Addison have been holding down the fort at edge without Stewart, and Addison already has a couple of sacks.

At defensive tackle, veteran Gabe Brownlow-Dindy is out with an injury, and former Tide reserve Kelby Collins is slated to get the starting nod. Collins was a bit of a tweener that couldn't carve a role for himself last year, so it'll be interesting to see how he holds up.

At linebacker, former Tide reserve Justin Okoronkwo was exceptional for USC last year and now leads the Gamecocks in tackles so far this season. He's a highly athletic linebacker that I still hate left Alabama, as he was an excellent special teamer as a freshman and I thought he'd be in line to be a starter for Alabama this year had he stayed. Fred Johnson and Shawn Murphy also both return from last year.

In the secondary, cornerback Vicari Swain returns and is getting his first real shot at being a full time starting cornerback after being an All-SEC punt returner a year ago. Opposite him Judge Collier returns after being a regular contributing piece the last couple of years, as does safety Peyton Williams. Interestingly, all 5 of USCs starting defensive backs are players that have been with USC their whole careers – none from the transfer portal.

This South Carolina defense has given Alabama fits the last two seasons, and they return their coaches and a lot of the players from last year's roster. I do think their defensive line has dropped off a little bit, and starting Kelby Collins as an undersized defensive tackle could come back to bite them if Alabama goes heavy with the run game. On top of that, we still don't know just how much Dylan Stewart is going to be ready in what is essentially his first full game in nearly a year.

They have an active linebacker group that can cause some problems, too. So don't be surprised if Alabama has some struggles with short passing game or perimeter runs. On the other hand, the secondary was highly suspect against Mississippi State last week. Was it a one-off bad game for them? Or is it a weak link for the defense? That one remains to be seen, as we overall don't have a lot of data points on them just yet.

I think this one will be a tough go of things for the Alabama offense. More so just based on the last two seasons than anything specifically. Ultimately, the Tide is able to prevail and move the ball enough (especially with interior runs) to keep things moving. Let's go with 31 points for the Tide.

articles.title: New-look squad, but how will Pocognoli's Scotland line-up?
articles.summary: Former Scotland forwards James McFadden and Pat Nevin try to guess who new head coach Sebastien Pocognoli will pick to start in Slovenia on Saturday.
articles.body:
Showtime is fast approaching for Sebastien Pocognoli 's Scotland .

The Tartan Army are taking over the Slovenian capital of Ljubljana and their heroes will join them later on Friday when they fly in from La Manga for Saturday's opening Nations League game.

Scotland's new head coach took a fair few fresh faces out to Spain , something that earned him early kudos from supporters who were calling for a bit of shake-up in the squad - but how does that translate to his team?

Adding eight uncapped players to a 27-man squad - before releasing Findlay Curtis and James Wilson to the under-21s - is one thing, but will the line-up reflect such a shift when it drops on the national team's social media channels on Saturday afternoon?

Former Scotland winger Pat Nevin thinks it would be "slightly bizarre" to see any more than two uncapped starters, while his fellow ex-international, James McFadden , insists the team will look "pretty similar" without any "big surprises".

So is it a case of the more things change, the more they stay the same for Scotland?

Hickey 'to drive' team forward from centre-back?

Going by what we know of Pocognoli's past, many are leading with the assumption he will play a back-three in defence.

The addition of Stephen Welsh , Luke Graham and Luis Binks - all new to the Scotland set-up - perhaps offers a sneak-peak as to what could come further down the line, but for now, will it be a more tried and trusted trio?

Jack Hendry and Scott McKenna - although the latter now does have left-footed competition in Graham and Binks - appear to be favoured by most, but what of the the right centre-back?

McFadden thinks pushing Brentford right-back Aaron Hickey there will help "drive" the team forward.

"I hope the centre-backs aren't the players on the team who have the ball the most," the former Scotland forward said on the BBC's Scottish Football Podcast.

"I don't want to see this centre-back to centre-back play. If they're getting it, I want them to drive and I think, if you had Hickey as a right-centre-back, he'd be driving into the play and trying to commit to going forward.

"I don't want them just sitting in a safe position, playing around the back. I don't want to see that, it's boring."

'If Gilmour's not playing, I'm going home'

One player who is seldom boring for Scotland is Billy Gilmour .

The midfielder's presence was missed at the World Cup, but after signing off from Serie A at the weekend with a goal for Napoli , he is returning ready to go.

Nevin will be making a swift exit from the Stozice Stadium if Gilmour is not starting - where he will surely be beside Lewis Ferguson .

"One of, if not the best player for us at the World Cup," McFadden said of the Bologna captain, who will surely look to his left and find captain Andy Robertson at wing-back.

"You're not going to go and change the midfield up. I don't think there's a need for a change for change's sake.

"I think that the freshness was needed, but I'm just looking forward to seeing them actually play and see if there's any difference in how they approach it - if they are more aggressive in a press and more dominant with possession."

At times, Scotland have struggled to get the Aston Villa captain in his best position in midfield - and yet he still never fails to perform.

With Scott McTominay missing from the squad as he recovers from successful minor heart surgery, Nevin suggested: "We need his explosiveness in the final third, so I would like to see him a little bit further forward."

It is the same old names so far - with Bournemouth winger Ben Gannon-Doak operating somewhere down the right, dependent on Hickey's position - but we do know there will need to be a new-ish name up top of sorts.

Even still, the favourite to lead the line is 16-time capped, Oli McBurnie.

His exile from international football does mean he feels like a new addition - as does his words about his desire to perform on his long-awaited return.

"He's coming back with a point to prove, which I like," McFadden said.

"You've got someone who will give their all, which is how Oli plays anyway, and he'll feel privileged that he's got the opportunity to play again.

"It's a big opportunity, because over the last couple of years we've been so used to seeing Che Adams , Lyndon Dykes and Lawrence Shankland , so it'll be nice to see a bit of freshness up there."

That all leaves one spot up for grabs and, in this case, it's on the left of the front three. And Bournemouth's Ryan Christie is familiar with that responsibility.

articles.title: ‘They don’t want trans people to exist’ – Lynx’s Cheryl Reeve speaks her mind
articles.summary: Minnesota Lynx head coach Cheryl Reeve isn’t backing down from her public support of the transgender community. Minnesota Lynx coach Cheryl Reeve has long us...
articles.body:
Minnesota Lynx head coach Cheryl Reeve isn't backing down from her public support of the transgender community.

Minnesota Lynx coach Cheryl Reeve has long used her platform to champion progressive causes and stand up for LGBTQ+ rights.

During an August matchup against the Indiana Fever , a game surrounded by tension following anti-trans remarks from opponents, Reeve made a quiet statement on the sidelines by wearing a "Trans Kids Belong" shirt beneath her jacket.

Meanwhile, the league faces external pressure to tighten its rules. Critics and political figures are pushing to explicitly restrict play to biological females, targeting the current collective bargaining agreement that simply states eligibility for "players who are women".

Cheryl Reeve stands up for the transgender community

Minnesota Lynx coach Cheryl Reeve isn't holding back on her support for the trans community. Looking back on the season, she doubled down on her stance, calling the pushback against trans youth an outright attack on their right to exist, and insisting that showing support is a matter of life and death.

She said: "I think that's probably one of the more meaningful things that would mark the season for me. It's that the transgender community is one that deserves our support and what is happening in the name of some issues of transgender in sports. It's really an attack on all transgender community, they don't want transgender people to exist.

"So I think that the amount of communication of that people who were affected by something as simple as wearing a T-shirt in support of them and helping them be seen. With the platform that we have in professional sports, it was a small gesture by me, it's something I believe in obviously whole heartedly and so if I could have helped just one to feel differently about themselves because for the transgender community this really is about life and death for them.

"The number of parents of transgender kids that I heard from and how it helped them and their families, it helped their child think differently about themselves and that there is someone in our position like we have as a leader. To know that there are people out there that believe in them, that they belong."

The thing that makes things so difficult for the WNBA is the difference in opinion. For example, if they shut the door on transgender athletes, they risk upsetting people like Cheryl, but on the flip side, if they don't ban transgender athletes, then it opens up even more issues.

articles.title: The Rochester Red Wings win their first International League title since 1997
articles.summary: The Washington Nationals AAA affiliate won a league title. This is a sign of the progress the new regime is making
articles.body:
The Washington Nationals brought home a championship! Well, not exactly, but the organization did bring home some hardware yesterday. The Rochester Red Wings, the Nats AAA affiliate, won their first International League title since 1997 last night. They won a winner take all game 3 over the Memphis Red Birds to be crowned champions.

When Paul Toboni became the Nationals President of Baseball Operations last year, he talked extensively about building a player development monster. You can see that monster roaring in the minor leagues, where Nats affiliates have had a lot of success. However, no team has had a bigger turnaround than the Red Wings.

Last season, Rochester was the worst team in the International League, with a 59-88 record. Since becoming a Nationals affiliate in 2021, the Red Wings only finished above .500 once before this season. Obviously minor league records are not everything, but with Triple-A being one step away from the big leagues, I think it does show something.

In the past, the Nats simply did not have the depth. There were not capable bodies ready to answer the call when needed. This season that has changed and the record is not the only way to see that. Andrew Alvarez, Andres Chaparro, Dylan Crews , Brady House , Erik Tolman, Jack Sinclair and Yohandy Morales all spent time in AAA this year, but when they came up, those guys have been largely ready for the moment.

Obviously, not everyone that has come up from Rochester has been great, but we have seen the fruits of Rochester's great season in some ways. This season, the Red Wings went 90-58 and capped things off with a dramatic title win. The Wings came back from 2-1 down with an 8th inning rally spearheaded by Andrew Pinckney . Eddy Yean closed things out in the 9th, and the Red Wings became champions.

However, the job is not quite finished for Matt LeCroy's bunch. The Red Wings head to Las Vegas for a chance to become Triple-A champions on Sunday. They square off with the Oklahoma City Comets, the Dodgers affiliate in a winner take all contest. The game is at 10 PM, but it will be something to monitor.

There have been a lot of stars on the Red Wings team, some of which could be big names for the Nats. Since his promotion to Rochester in May, Seaver King has been one of the team's star players. He hit .289 with an .858 OPS in 77 games for the Red Wings. King also played a key role in the series win over the Red Birds which included a home run in game one of the series.

The Wings also have familiar faces who are looking for a second chance in the big leagues. Riley Adams and Trey Lipscomb have both been huge parts of Rochester's success this year. We will see if that translates to the big leagues, but it is nice to see them doing well.

Back in August, I actually went up to Rochester to take a closer look at this team and speak to some of the key figures. I came away very impressed with the culture that manager Matt LeCroy has built up there. It is also clear that the AAA team and the big league club are more aligned than ever before. Here is that piece if you want to take a look.

LeCroy has played a massive role in shaping this ball club. He is a charismatic leader who his players absolutely adore. The longtime Red Wings manager has a combination of charm and coaching skill that is hard to find.

However, you also have to credit the new regime. LeCroy has been around for a long time, but he has never had this kind of success before. Paul Toboni has placed an emphasis on development and winning at all levels. That is shining through in Rochester.

As we move forward, hopefully this Minor League success can translate to winning at the big league level. An International League title is one thing, but the main goal is a World Series title. To be fair, we have seen more success in the big leagues this year as well.

The Nats have their most wins since 2019 and with one more victory, they will avoid last place. At all levels of the organization, it seems like things are trending in the right direction. That is the first time you can say that in a long time.

Paul Toboni and the new regime have not had a perfect year one, but you can see the vision. Between the offensive success in the big leagues and the wins on the farm, the Nats are now upwardly mobile. Now it is time to see if the Red Wings can finish the job and win the Triple-A World Series.

articles.title: Lamine Yamal opens up on his personal growth and maturity: ‘The happier I am, the better I perform’
articles.summary: At 19 years old, FC Barcelona prodigy Lamine Yamal has established himself as one of the best footballers in the globe. The teenage sensation has already tas...
articles.body:
At 19 years old, FC Barcelona prodigy Lamine Yamal has established himself as one of the best footballers in the globe.

The teenage sensation has already tasted enormous success both at the club level and the international level, most recently winning the 2026 FIFA World Cup with Spain.

Now, he is one of the strongest contenders to win the Ballon d'Or , the biggest individual honour in football.

Given his meteoric rise at a tender age, Lamine attracts a lot of attention and pressure. But the youngster has shown great maturity and personal growth, having had to progress through such stages at a very early phase in his career.

In a recent interview with TVE (h/t SPORT ), the La Masia forward acknowledged that he is becoming more professional and focused on becoming the best player in the game.

"I am being more professional, and that was something that was a little difficult for me too. In the end, when you are 17 there are things that, when you are 19, you say, 'I have to be like this'," explained Lamine.

One of the best in the world. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

"I think you can notice it," Lamine added when discussing his maturity and his greater personal balance.

"The happier I am, the better I perform," admitted the Barcelona academy graduate, who is currently with the Spain squad as they begin their UEFA Nations League campaign.

On Barcelona's new signings and start to the season

Lamine also praised the Barcelona team, particularly the new arrivals, who have adapted quickly to Hansi Flick's ways.

"Gordon, who has fitted in very well, Rodri , Adeyemi… they are performing at a very high level," the teenager said.

"We have arrived in very good physical condition," he added, highlighting another feature of Barça's impressive start to the season.

Lamine very happy with the start Barcelona have made. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

Continuing, Lamine noted: "The more time the manager spends with us, the more we understand each other, and the players do too."

Staying away from Real Madrid 's controversies

Lamine Yamal also demonstrated the maturity he had been discussing by refusing to get involved in the latest controversies surrounding Real Madrid, including the disputes involving Jose Mourinho and the club's conflicts with journalists and referees.

For Lamine, the priority is Barcelona and enjoying the team's current form.

"I am not really following it, to be honest. I am not very interested. As long as Barça keep winning, there is nothing to talk about, only our football and our victories," he said.

The Barcelona forward is therefore keeping his focus on his own team and its strong collective start to the campaign, rather than becoming involved in the issues surrounding their rivals.
